title: Green Card Tool - Freshness Fetch Results
description: Structured output that a Claude-assisted FETCH session produces during Step 1 of the monthly freshness workflow. IMPORTANT: a bare cron/Python script CANNOT produce this file. travel.state.gov and uscis.gov are Cloudflare-walled (they 403 both scripts and headless browsers). The only working fetch path is Claude's WebFetch tool against tier-2 law-firm aggregators (which a cron has no access to). So this JSON is the HAND-OFF ARTIFACT between the (Claude-assisted, not pure-cron) fetch step and the mechanical diff/apply steps. The harness (diff_proposal.py) CONSUMES this file; it never scrapes to produce it. See RUNBOOK.md Step 1 for the exact fetch prompt.

run_date.description: The canonical date of this freshness run, YYYY-MM-DD. This becomes the proposal filename and meta.last_verified on apply. Set it explicitly so runs are reproducible - do NOT rely on wall-clock time.

bulletin_month_found.description: The Visa Bulletin month the fetch session actually found live on the sources, e.g. '2026-08' or '2026-09'. If the next month's bulletin is not yet published on any source, report the current live month here and note it in the finding-level notes.

fetched_by.description: Optional. Who/what ran the fetch, e.g. 'claude-websession-2026-09-10' or 'manual'. For the audit trail only.

fetch_notes.description: Optional free-text run-level notes: which tier-1 sources 403-blocked (expected), whether the next month was published, aggregator disagreements, etc.

findings.description: One entry per rulebook field the fetch session gathered a value for. Only include fields the SOP marks in-scope. Do NOT include fields whose source is auto_fetchable:false (uscis-processing-times) unless you are recording a deliberate could-not-verify note; the harness will skip them regardless.

field_path.description: Dot path into rulebook.json, e.g. 'bulletin.categories.EB-2.India.final_action_date'. Category cells live under bulletin.categories.<EB-1|EB-2|EB-3>.<India|China|ROW|Mexico|Philippines>.<final_action_date|date_for_filing|status_note>. Use null-denotes-unavailable and the string 'CURRENT' verbatim per the rulebook convention.

found_value.description: The value observed on the source(s), in the SAME shape the rulebook stores. A date string 'YYYY-MM-DD', the literal string 'CURRENT', null for UNAVAILABLE/'U', a number, or a [low, high] range array. NEVER invent single-value precision from a range (per SOP 2.3).

sources.description: Source ids from sources.json (e.g. 'travel-state-visa-bulletin', 'murthy-visa-bulletin', 'fragomen-visa-bulletin'). At least one. Per SOP: a tier-1 success OR two tier-2 sources in agreement is required to pass. A single tier-2 source alone is low confidence.

tier.description: The BEST tier among the sources that agreed on this value. 1 = government primary (travel.state.gov, flag.dol.gov, uscis). 2 = law-firm aggregator. 3 = community. The verified:false -> true transition is only allowed when tier == 1.

confidence.description: high = structured data (table cell) with exact match, or tier-1 confirmation. medium = regex over prose OR two tier-2 sources in agreement. low = inferred/computed/ambiguous OR single tier-2 source. LOW findings are REJECTED by the harness (listed under could-not-verify), never auto-merged.

notes.description: Optional. Source snippet, raw excerpt, aggregator disagreement detail, or reasoning. The proposal carries this through for human review.

examples.fetch_notes: travel.state.gov 403-blocked as expected; used Murthy + Fragomen for tier-2 agreement. September 2026 bulletin was live.

findings.notes: Two aggregators agree; unchanged from prior month. Example of a no_change finding.
Currently null in rulebook -> this is new_coverage. Two tier-2 sources agree so it clears the auto-merge bar; verified flag stays false (tier 2, not tier 1).
Example verification_transition: EB-2 India FAD was null (Unavailable, verified:false candidate). A tier-1 confirmation both fills the value AND authorizes flipping verified:false -> true.
